translation_notes: prefixes: RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, plus the two ns_def_local locals ontosyn and ontospecies (both Namespace("...") built inside the function body), all as @prefix declarations.

Both local namespaces are only ever used through attribute access (ontosyn.hasChemicalOutput, ontospecies.Species, ontospecies.hasProductName) to build terms, never passed around as objects, so no `as NAME` binding is needed.

_select_uris is called by the original but not defined in the extracted lines (163/1196 case): added species_context.py, a minimal shim reconstructing it as a plain SELECT-?uri runner, imported identically by original.py and translated.ldpy.
The embedded PREFIX ontosyn:/ontospecies: lines inside the f-string SPARQL query text (sparql_literal, not this stratum) are left untouched.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the query goes straight into `_select_uris` (no `q`); `_normalize_product_name` becomes one `str(value).strip().lower().removesuffix(" synthesis").strip()` and takes the label itself (its callers always passed `str(label)`, and `str(value or "")` of a str is the str); the two target-name loops become one set comprehension over the property path `(ontosyn.hasChemicalOutput * "?") / RDFS.label` (the labels of synth and of its outputs), minus "" (the `if norm:` filter: an empty name can then never meet on the species side, so the species side needs no filter); `seen`, `_add_species` and the nested species loops become one loop over `subject_objects(RDFS.label | ontospecies.hasProductName)` filtered by the rdf:type membership, deduplicated by an insertion-ordered dict keyed by `URIRef(str(species))` (the original deduplicated on the same string). The `if not target_names: return` guard survives (`return []`, the empty `resolved`).

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the f-string SPARQL text pasting `<{synth}>` becomes `s{ }` with `{synth}` as an initial binding, its PREFIX lines inherited from the `@prefix` declarations (`_select_uris` hands it to graph.query unchanged); the two Namespace objects go (module-level `@prefix`); the path is interpolated in the predicate position of `m{ }`, with prefixed names as operands; the species loop is one two-pattern `m{ ?species a ontospecies:Species ; {rdfs:label | ontospecies:hasProductName} ?name }` (the Python side does the same join with a membership test, so no exception to the symmetry rule); `URIRef(str(species))` becomes `f<{species}>` (no @base in scope).
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: of `typing` only List is used: `from typing import List`; the rdflib imports are all used.

optimized_header.ldpy: `from typing import List`; Namespace, RDF and RDFS go, and `@prefix rdf:` too (`a` replaces rdf:type); `from rdflib import Graph, URIRef` stays for the signature, with the rdfs:, ontosyn: and ontospecies: prefixes.
